name: Bohemian
basis: a decor style: nested arches, warm tint, pale sun, pampas grass (how)

lumenary.blurb: Boho colour: earthy rainbow arches, a sun, warm tones and pampas grass.

facts.from: Artistic circles of 19th century Paris, revived in the 1960s and 70s
facts.bestOn: Warm portraits, weddings and sunlit scenes

why: The bohemian look is soft, earthy and handmade: terracotta, sage and cream, rounded shapes and dried grasses. The rainbow arch has become its symbol, so the picture here is framed in a window of nested arches, warmed by a pale orange glow and finished with a low sun and feathery pampas grass.
how: Show the photograph inside an arch shaped window.
Draw arches around it, each wider than the last by a fixed gap, taking colours in turn from an earthy palette.
Warm the photograph by multiplying it with a pale orange and a faint brown.
Draw a pale sun with rays behind the arches and a row of dots for the ground.
Fan curved strokes with small feathery ellipses at each side as pampas grass.
history: The word bohemian was first used in France in the nineteenth century for artists and writers who lived outside convention, and was made famous by stories such as Henri Murger’s tales of Parisian artists. Its modern revival in fashion and interiors began in the 1960s and 70s and returned strongly in the 2010s, together with arches and pampas grass.
uses: Nursery and living room wall prints
terms: A way of laying one colour over another so that the result is never lighter than either.
A tall grass with soft, feathery plumes, popular in boho décor.
A curved top over an opening, repeated here as nested rings.
paragraphs: Boho colour is earthy and soft, and its signature shape is the rainbow arch. The picture is shown inside an arch window, and the arches around it get wider by a fixed gap each ring and take their colours in turn from an earthy palette. A warm tone is laid over the photograph by multiplying it with a pale orange, then a faint brown on top.

A pale sun with rays sits behind the arches, a row of dots marks the ground, and the pampas grass at each side is a fan of curved strokes with small feathery ellipses along their outer half, each one randomly longer or shorter.

equations.note: Radius of ring i: the window radius plus i times the gap g.
Multiply blend with the tint T; the blend strength a follows the warm tone slider.

presets.text: Sage with six rings is a calm, garden palette.
Rose without the sun is more modern and minimal.
Full warmth gives a golden-hour finish.
